filters.purpose: Read the SHA-pinned public Small IN100 processed mesh and its original feature/pair tables. This is an existing prepared network, not a fresh reconstruction or proof of identity with the paper mesh. Retain the imported data for comparison; physical calibration must be established separately from normalized distribution weights.
Mark the 12 zero-area source triangles. Their normals are undefined; the mask is a geometric validity check, not a minimum-area cutoff or removal of small physical boundaries.

Remove only degenerate triangles and compact vertices, transferring paired grain labels, original interface ID, and node types. All 4224 internal grain pairs remain represented; the supplied unique-pair table remains valid for metric uncertainty counts. Recompute areas and normals after geometry selection.

Recompute nonzero triangle areas from the retained geometry. MRD normalization uses relative area weights; a common length-scale factor cancels. Do not interpret source numeric coordinates as calibrated meters from the imported default unit tag.

Recompute finite unit normals from the same triangle winding and retained vertices. Preserve the correspondence between normals and the two face labels; arbitrary normal/label changes can alter crystallographic interpretation.

Compute the area-weighted binned five-parameter distribution for the retained same-phase internal boundaries. Resolution 10 degrees follows the paper nominal coarse-bin comparison scale; the native partition is not a uniform angular neighborhood or a claim of identical paper bins. More bins require more independent boundary data; mesh triangles are not independent grain boundaries.

Probe the binned distribution at the Sigma3 misorientation: angle first, [60,1,1,1]. The 128-pixel stereographic grid is a display sampling choice, not extra experimental resolution. Its coordinates are dimensionless projection coordinates despite the current image unit metadata.

Export the same fixed-misorientation binned section on the writer sampling grid. Input is angle-axis [60,1,1,1]; the text header writes axis-angle. Use actual angular coordinates rather than assuming text rows correspond to image pixels.

Export retained positive-label internal triangles with both grain orientations, face normal and area for independent boundary-analysis tools. Areas are in the source coordinate scale squared, whose absolute physical calibration is not established by this converted fixture. Preserve the matching Euler/normal reference convention.

Probe Sigma3 using the metric method with 3-degree misorientation and 7-degree plane radii, matching the paper radius choice but on this different prepared network. Input order differs from the binned filters: axis then angle [1,1,1,60]. Keep triple-line triangles for the same baseline population. Save absolute sampling errors, not confidence in physical reconstruction.

Compute the marginal boundary-plane distribution with a 7-degree cap over all eligible same-phase boundaries, without fixing a misorientation. This is not another Sigma3 section. Retain triple-line triangles consistently and use the verified original unique-pair table, not the triangle count, for error estimates.

Save source context, validated reduced mesh, binned GBCD and its stereographic section. Metric methods produce named text files alongside this checkpoint. No original paper peak, material acceptance threshold, or physical-area calibration is claimed.
